security_spec.violation_condition: XiangShan decoder has no entry for REV (funct12=0x69f RV32 / 0x6bf RV64 under OP-IMM+funct3=0x5). The existing ALU datapath only supports byte-level bit-reverse (revb/BREV8 at ALUOpType.revb) and byte-level byte-swap (rev8/REV8 at ALUOpType.rev8), but has no full-XLEN bit-reverse operation. When the decoder encounters these funct12 values, either an illegal-instruction exception fires where it should not (DoS for P-ext software) or the pattern collides with a different instruction due to undriven decode defaults, silently producing wrong results. Additionally, no XLEN-aware encoding selection logic exists to distinguish the RV32-only funct12 (0x69f) from the RV64-only funct12 (0x6bf), so a misconfigured or incorrectly-constrained Chisel decode table could map both to the same (wrong) micro-op.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: funct12 == 0x69f || funct12 == 0x6bf || REV || full bit reverse XLEN || Cat(Reverse(src1))
security_spec.summary: P-ext REV (full-XLEN bit-reverse) has no decoder entry and no ALU datapath in XiangShan; RV32 (funct12=0x69f) and RV64 (funct12=0x6bf) encodings differ but no XLEN-aware decode logic exists, risking illegal-exception DoS or silent wrong-result execution.

findings.finding: BitmanipDecode table has no entry for P-ext REV (funct12=0x69f RV32 / 0x6bf RV64). REV8 (Zbb byte-swap, funct12=0x6b8) is decoded at line 339, and BREV8 (Zbkb byte-bit-reverse, funct12=0x687) at line 361, but the full-XLEN bit-reverse instruction is absent. When P-ext software issues REV, the decoder falls through to decodeDefault (line 50-61), which sets SelImm.INVALID_INSTR, triggering illegalInstr. This is a confirmed DoS for any software ported to the P-ext REV instruction — correct programs will crash. However, there is NO silent data corruption because the decoder's default path is properly wired to fire an illegal-instruction exception rather than producing wrong results.

ALUOpType defines revb (BREV8, per-byte bit-reverse), rev8 (REV8, byte-swap), pack, and orh48 in the 'b101_xxxx' group. No 'rev' operation exists for full-XLEN bit-reverse. Open encoding slots at 'b101_0100' through 'b101_0111' are available for adding a rev opcode without restructuring the encoding space.
findings.snippet:
def revb       = "b101_0000".U
def rev8       = "b101_0001".U
def pack       = "b101_0010".U
def orh48      = "b101_0011".U
// no rev at "b101_0100"

findings.finding: The ALU computes revb (per-byte bit-reverse: Cat of 8 Reverse operations, one per byte, re-assembled in MSB-to-LSB order) and rev8 (byte-swap: Cat of 8 byte-slices reordered LSB-to-MSB). No full-XLEN bit-reverse (Cat(Reverse(src1)) or similar across all 64 bits) is computed. Even if a decode entry were added, the datapath does not produce the correct result.
findings.snippet:
val revb = Cat((0 until 8).map(i => Reverse(src1(8 * i + 7, 8 * i))).reverse)
val pack = Cat(src2(31, 0), src1(31, 0))
val rev8 = Cat((0 until 8).map(i => src1(8 * i + 7, 8 * i)))
// no val rev = Reverse(src1) for P-ext REV

findings.finding: MiscResultSelect.revRes is a 4-entry VecInit using func(1,0) to select among (revb, rev8, pack, orh48). No 5th entry for a full-bit-reverse operation. Adding a rev opcode requires widening this selection or using a different select mechanism.
findings.snippet: val revRes = VecInit(Seq(io.revb, io.rev8, io.pack, io.orh48))(io.func(1, 0))

findings.finding: REV8 BitPat (line 334: b011010111000) encodes Zbb REV8 byte-swap at funct12=0x6b8, not P-ext REV at funct12=0x6bf. P-ext REV's RV64 encoding at funct12=0x6bf (b011010111111) and RV32 encoding at funct12=0x69f (b011010011111) are not defined anywhere in Scala sources. No 'REV' BitPat identifier exists in the codebase.
findings.snippet: def REV8 = BitPat("b011010111000?????101?????0010011")  // funct12=0x6b8 (REV8, not P-ext REV at 0x6bf)

findings.finding: The decoder's fallback path (decodeDefault) correctly flags unmatched instructions as illegal by setting SelImm.INVALID_INSTR. This default is propagated to exceptionII (line 877-878) which triggers illegalInstr. This is the correct RISC-V behavior for unimplemented instructions and prevents silent wrong-result execution. The silent-corruption scenario hypothesized in the security spec (undriven decode defaults mapping to wrong micro-ops) is NOT present in this RTL.
findings.snippet:
def decodeDefault: List[BitPat] = // illegal instruction
  List(SrcType.X, SrcType.X, SrcType.X, FuType.X, FuOpType.X, N, N, N, N, N, N, N, UopSplitType.X, SelImm.INVALID_INSTR)
